data.description:
The new iPhone 13 mini offers one of the best displays of high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and the front. However, not all damage to the display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone 13 mini have reported a sudden black screen with no prior damage history. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 13 mini is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone is running okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. The phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The phone's display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus) 

The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone. (Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen) 

Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect to any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended, however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issues. It might be risky for any layman. 

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving No light on display issues on your iPhone 13 mini. We are a service center that operates based on 4 different and convenient points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 Mini comes with a distinct feature called Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues, however, have some home remedies that may work for your iPhone. These fixed attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

if you use a screen protector, make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.

Make sure you are facing the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID, instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

The user might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked with face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 13 mini offers its users better optimization and balance in software than previous iPhone models. However, no matter how hard they try, there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning.The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it gets stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on the Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has caused some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

Update disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity

It is rare, however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues, however, can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps to see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 13 mini

(Press the volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 13 mini power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, You may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS app to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

data.description:

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone 13 Mini comes with upgraded network connectivity compared to previous iPhone models and supports 5G network connectivity. Despite technological advancements from previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone 13 Mini network connectivity. Such as loss of the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues, however, are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding networks in iPhone 13 Mini are:

iPhone 13 Mini gets down to 0 network bars randomly

Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G

Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company

Network never reaches the full level

These common issues, however, can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone 13 Mini. To resolve this, Apple recommends its iPhone 13 Mini users some DIY (do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. -requires a restart of the device

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set it up, go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network.

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to be checked by a professional technician. data.description:
The new iPhone 13 mini is a smartphone that has a lot of ambient sensors such as an accelerometer, a gyroscopic sensor, and a proximity sensor. The proximity sensor is probably the most used on your iPhone. This sensor is used for turning your phone’s screen off when it is placed near your face during a phone call. So that it may conserve battery or avoid unnecessary touch inputs by your face when talking. It may also be used for features like “Raise and Wake” and other minimal yet handy features.

However, you may face problems with the proximity sensor of your iPhone 13 Mini over time. Some issues with the iPhone 13 mini proximity sensor reported by users of the iPhone 13 mini in the users' community are:

The proximity sensor is not working/ too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls

The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call

The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone 13 mini proximity sensor. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

Try removing your screen protector, which may block the proximity sensors' proper working

Restart your iPhone

Update your iOS
